findings.problem: BudgetWorkflow uses flat booleans (is_validated, is_sent) instead of a typestate enum, so callers can construct states like is_validated=false with is_sent=true that no legitimate workflow should ever allow
findings.failure_mode: illegal state BudgetWorkflow{is_validated:false, is_sent:true} is representable and silently propagates through the system, causing double-sends or unsent-but-marked-valid budgets
findings.fix: Replace is_validated and is_sent with a single BudgetState enum (e.g., Draft, Validated, Sent) with a smart constructor that enforces legal transitions; remove both bool fields

findings.problem: status is a public String field set to arbitrary string literals; mark_sent hardcodes "sent" via .to_string() instead of using a domain enum variant
findings.failure_mode: callers can set status to any string (e.g., "sent!", "", "SENT", or a null byte), breaking downstream pattern matching, serialization, and audit trails; "sent" is also redundant with is_sent=true
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a BudgetStatus enum {Draft, Validated, Sent, Rejected}; remove the redundant is_sent field; make the enum derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a standalone lifecycle flag; it can be true while is_sent is also true (double-send) or both false (no lifecycle progress tracked), with no invariant enforcement
findings.failure_mode: a budget can be marked both validated and sent simultaneously, or neither, with no guard; downstream code has no way to prove the workflow is in a legal state without re-implementing the state machine
findings.fix: Fold lifecycle into the typestate enum: BudgetState::Validated carries any validated metadata; BudgetState::Sent carries sent_at_epoch_ms; BudgetState::Draft carries nothing; remove both is_validated and is_sent

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is an optional lifecycle field on the struct alongside flat booleans, creating combinations like is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None or is_sent=false with Some(epoch)
findings.failure_mode: a budget can be is_sent=true with no epoch recorded (unauditable) or is_sent=false with a valid epoch (stale ghost data); the Option is decoupled from the boolean that controls its interpretation
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant: BudgetState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }; remove the Option<u64> field and is_sent bool entirely

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain semantics, validation, or formatting guarantees; any string value including empty, whitespace, or malicious input is accepted
findings.failure_mode: budgets can be created with empty or duplicate IDs, colliding with external systems or violating uniqueness constraints; no parse boundary exists to reject hostile input
findings.fix: Replace with a newtype: pub struct BudgetId(String); add a smart constructor BudgetId::from_str(s) that rejects empty/whitespace and returns a typed ParseError; make id private or expose only through methods

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts a raw BudgetWorkflow struct with public String and bool fields; there is no parse boundary or smart constructor that validates inputs before the core accepts them, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.failure_mode: any caller can instantiate BudgetWorkflow{status:"", is_validated:false, is_sent:false, sent_at_epoch_ms:null} and pass it to mark_sent, which silently sets status to "sent" and is_sent to true without any validation — the boundary between shell and core is completely absent
findings.fix: Introduce a smart constructor BudgetWorkflow::new(id: BudgetId) -> Self that sets the initial state; mark_sent should accept BudgetWorkflow and return Result<BudgetWorkflow, BudgetError>; the parse boundary converts raw primitives at the shell into the trusted domain type once
